text:
sarah: Hey team — running into a hard blocker on the Acme POC. Their network team says the PrivateEndpoint to our hosted API fails TLS handshake intermittently and the app falls back to 502/connection reset. They also sent a security questionnaire asking about KMS key usage and logs retention, and commercial asked for Dedicated POC pricing. Need quick triage and owners.

raj: Can you paste the client-side logs and the server error traces you have? Also which endpoint hostname are they resolving?

sarah: Client log snippet from their dev:```
curl: (35) error:14077410:SSL routines:SSL23_GET_SERVER_HELLO:sslv3 alert handshake failure
POST /v1/generate 502 
remote_addr=10.0.2.14
server: redwood-inference-01
```
They say the DNS resolves to vpce-0a1b2c3d-abc.us-east-1.vpce.amazonaws.com but their app uses custom hostname redwood.acme.internal.

nic: That smells like SNI/hostname mismatch — PrivateLink interface endpoints do hostname rewriting if they don't enable private DNS. If the cert CN is the internal vpce hostname but client sends SNI redwood.acme.internal, handshake will fail. Can you confirm the cert presented?

sarah: We grabbed a broken handshake capture — server cert subject: CN=vpce-0a1b2c3d-abc.us-east-1.vpce.amazonaws.com, SAN includes that only. Customer expected redwood.acme.internal and they created a private hosted zone mapping to the interface endpoint.

olivia: Also seeing high 429s in our edge logs for that account during the POC window — looks like their test harness was running at 200 rps, hitting our standard burst limits. Snippet:```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-rate-limit: 180/60
retry-after: 25
```
We should offer a temporary quota bump for the POC and ask them to throttle tests.

mike: On pricing — for a two-week Dedicated proof we can do a short-term commit with prorated monthly rate or keep them on hosted with a usage credit. I'll prepare numbers but sales needs the blocker cleared first. I can take the pricing action.

raj: Actionable next steps from infra/runtime side: 1) Confirm whether customer enabled "Enable for Private DNS" when creating interface endpoint. If not, their private hosted zone won't rewrite SNI — they need the endpoint cert to match the hostname or we need to add a SAN (not ideal). 2) If they insist on custom hostname, route recommendation: use a VPC endpoint + resolver rule pointing to our service DNS and ensure the client SNI equals cert CN.

nic: Short-term mitigation: instruct their network team to use the vpce hostname as the SNI/Host value in the client, or set up client-side override. Longer term: we can support a documented pattern for CNAME/ALIAS to vpce and certificate guidance.

infra-bot: deploy: branch poc-private-dns-fix -> staging completed at 1905001300 :white_check_mark:

sarah: Security Qs from their infosec: Do we support customer-managed KMS for data-at-rest? What log retention windows do you guarantee and can we provide SOC2/audit artifacts for the POC?

olivia: We support envelope encryption with customer-managed KMS on Private installs; for hosted we offer CMEK via our enterprise package and support audit logs export to their SIEM (S3/CloudTrail). Retention and artifacts are part of the contract — will coordinate with security.

mike: I'll take the security questionnaire answers and the provisional pricing.

raj: Volunteers for owners? I can own the cert/DNS triage and test a staging client override. Olivia can own the logs/quotas. Mike owns pricing & contract. Sarah will coordinate with the customer and collect confirmation from their network team.

sarah: Thanks — I'll ping the customer with two options: (A) quick client override using vpce SNI to unblock POC, plus temp quota bump; (B) longer-term DNS/private-hosted-zone fix with our docs. I'll loop in infosec for KMS details.

mike: If you need an SLA/commit for the POC let me know, I can attach a one-page term with temporary quota & support hours.

sarah: Great. Closing the loop here — will post customer confirmation when I have it. :thumbsup:
